title: Add real-time eval heartbeat and degradation detector
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: CI/eval pipelines catch functional regressions but often detect quality degradation only after user-visible impact. This PR introduces a lightweight real-time "heartbeat" probe plus an ensemble degradation detector to surface subtle run-time quality drift earlier and to provide a gradated CI response. Design summary: (1) Heartbeat poller: periodic low-overhead probe runner that executes a small canonical prompt-set across target model variants and captures compact signals (log-prob, token-level perplexity, response length, deterministic checksum of structured outputs). (2) Degradation detector: ensemble of three lightweight signals (historical z-score on log-prob, token-perplexity percentile shift, and structured-output schema entropy) plus an exponential smoothing window to reduce flapping. The detector outputs a composite score and a severity label (ok/warn/alert). (3) CI/operational integration: a new CI hook that runs the heartbeat as a fast pre-submit check for model/version changes, and a scheduled sentinel job that publishes metrics to the eval-metrics time-series and triggers Linear alerts when severity >= alert. Key behaviors: soft-fail for warn (post-comment and ticket suggestion), hard-fail for alert (blocks merge with explicit override required), automatic incident ticket creation for persistent alerts sustained over a configurable window. Implementation notes: added poller and detector logic in evh/heartbeat and evh/detectors, a small compatibility shim to run heartbeats against both hosted and private endpoints, and a new lightweight CI plugin under evh/ci/hooks that can be enabled per-repo. Rollout: default off in main; staged enablement via feature flag and canary on baseline models before full enforcement. Backwards compatibility: heartbeat is additive and opt-in; detector thresholds stored in CI config with sane defaults. Documentation: added operational runbook and runbook playbook entries. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration smoke against staging [x] documentation [x] Linear ticket created. Notes: this PR focuses on fast detection and avoids heavy eval runs; it is intentionally conservative about false positives.

review_comments: Diego: Can we reduce the heartbeat chattiness for high-frequency models? Author: Added adaptive backoff in poller config (heartbeat_defaults.yaml) to cap probes per-minute per-model. Laura: Detector thresholds look reasonable but we need better signal explainability in the PR UI. Author: Added a short summary field to detector output (primary contributing signal and delta) and included examples in docs. Omar: Are private endpoints supported? Author: Added private_endpoint_shim and tests; the hook will auto-detect endpoint type and pick credentials. Diego: Suggest adding a stable hash for structured outputs to detect semantic drift without full diffing. Author: Implemented checksum-based semantic fingerprint and included in metrics emitter.
release_notes: Add lightweight real-time heartbeat probe and ensemble degradation detector. New CI hook for fast pre-submit quality checks. Scheduled sentinel job that emits composite degradation metrics and creates incidents for sustained alerts. Opt-in rollout with feature flag; docs and runbook included.
testing_summary: unit: 68 tests (detector logic, smoothing, checksum) - all passing
integration: heartbeat against staging hosted/private endpoints - pass
load: synthetic smoke at 200 rps pulse for 1m to validate resource bounds - no impact observed
e2e: CI hook exercised in ephemeral environment; one flaky test retried and passed
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated. Canary on two low-traffic models for 48h; monitor composite score and SLO signals; if stable, enable on all evaluation pipelines in 7 days. Hard-fail gating will be disabled until 2 successful canaries.
motivation_short: Detect subtle quality regressions earlier with a low-cost continuous probe and reduce time-to-detect for production degradations.
